meta.title: Ferry Agent
meta.description: Get your books onto your e-reader. Runs at home, free book sources, delivery to Kindle, Kobo, Tolino and more.

hero.subtitle: Search for a book, add it to your library, send it to your device — simply.

howItWorks.title: How it works.
howItWorks.subtitle: Three steps: find a book, prepare it in your library, send it to your e-reader.

find.title: Find a book
find.body: Search by title or author. Open-access sources and your personal access, in one search.

prepare.title: Prepare it in your library
prepare.body: Add the book. It stays on your side, ready to send.

send.title: Send it to your e-reader
send.body: Choose the device. Ferry Agent handles the format and delivery.

mcpSpotlight.title: Your library, also from a conversation
mcpSpotlight.body: Search, add, and send your books from an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT…), with the same connection as the workspace.

selfHosted.q: Does this run on my machine?
selfHosted.a: Yes. The essentials and your library stay on your machine. Nothing is stored on servers we control.

gatewayNeeded.q: Do I need personal access to get started?
gatewayNeeded.a: Not for open-access books (Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks) and your own files. Personal access is only for sources set up on your machine.

readers.a: Kindle (email delivery), Kobo and cloud-linked devices, Tolino and browsers via a temporary code, and any e-reader connected over USB.

myData.a: Yes. Your library, your devices, your delivery history — everything stays with you.

agent.a: Yes. An AI assistant can search, add, and send for you, using the same connection as the workspace.

docs.metaDescription: Install your Ferry Agent personal access at home with Docker Desktop or OrbStack.
docs.title: Install your personal access
docs.intro: This guide follows the simple path: Docker Desktop or OrbStack, then import the provided file. In a few minutes, your access runs at home.
docs.pathChoice: Recommended path: the Docker Desktop or OrbStack interface. Advanced options (terminal) are at the bottom of the page.
docs.checklistItem1: Docker Desktop installed (or OrbStack on Mac)
docs.checklistItem2: A Ferry Agent account, so you can open the Access page
docs.checklistItem3: A few minutes to copy the two codes shown only once
docs.step1Action: Open the Access page, then click Add access. When it is created, note the connection code and the access key. Use the “Both codes together” block to copy everything at once — they will never be shown again.
docs.step1Success: Both codes appear once, with the “Both codes together” block.
docs.step2Action: Download the file with the button below. This is the file to import into Docker Desktop or OrbStack.
docs.step2UseFile: Keep this .tar file handy for the next step.
docs.step2Success: The download is complete on your computer.
docs.step3Title: Import the file in Docker Desktop or OrbStack
docs.step3Action: Open Docker Desktop or OrbStack. Import the .tar file you just downloaded, then wait until import finishes.
docs.step3Success: The Ferry Agent image appears in the Images list in Docker Desktop or OrbStack.
docs.step4Action: In Docker Desktop or OrbStack, start the imported image. Paste exactly the “Both codes together” block from Access (PAIRING_TOKEN and GATEWAY_KEY) into the startup settings that ask for them. Do not invent values, and do not leave blanks to fill in.
docs.step4Hint: Both codes are required. Without them, the Access page will stay waiting for a connection.
docs.step4Success: The program is running at home (started status in Docker Desktop or OrbStack).
docs.step5Action: Go back to the Access page in Ferry Agent. The status should become Connected.
docs.step5Success: On Access, the status shows Connected.
docs.afterBody: You can search for a book, add it to your library, then send it to your e-reader. For sources set up at home, also open the program’s local address (often http://127.0.0.1:9696) once Access is connected.
docs.afterMcp: For an AI assistant, add this address to Claude, ChatGPT, or your tool:
docs.closingLine: Find, prepare, send — your books follow this path to your e-reader.
docs.glossaryAccessDef: The program installed on your computer that links it to your Ferry Agent account.
docs.glossaryCodesDef: Two distinct codes, shown only once at creation. The “Both codes together” block groups them so you can paste PAIRING_TOKEN and GATEWAY_KEY as-is.
docs.glossaryProwlarrDef: The local screen that helps you connect extra search sources at home.
docs.glossaryIndexerDef: A site or catalog that lists books available to retrieve.
docs.troubleshootIntro: If something is stuck, start with these points:
docs.troubleshootWaiting: Access stays on “Waiting for the first connection”: check that the program is running in Docker Desktop or OrbStack, and that both codes are pasted there.
docs.troubleshootExpired: The code expired: on Access, click Create new codes, then update both codes in Docker Desktop or OrbStack.
docs.troubleshootOffline: Status Offline: restart the program at home. Your computer must stay on and connected to the internet.
docs.troubleshootBothCodes: One code is not enough. Always paste the “Both codes together” block (connection code + access key).
docs.terminalAltBody: If you prefer the terminal, start the already imported image and paste the real values from the “Both codes together” block (PAIRING_TOKEN and GATEWAY_KEY) as environment variables. Never replace them with sample values like CODE or KEY.
docs.terminalAltHint: Codes come only from the Access page, once at creation (or after Create new codes).
docs.byoDescription: Your personal access runs on your machine, not on our servers.
docs.byoBody1: Your computer must stay on and connected to the internet for searches and downloads to work.
docs.byoBody2: For 24/7 use, install the program on a machine that stays on, using the same two codes.
